designIntent.summary: Shared car-performance model used by preseason construction, permanent development, race packages, weekend setup and race simulation.
principles: Constructor identity does not determine starting performance.
All players build from the same fixed menu of car choices.
Car construction creates strengths and compromises rather than objectively best builds.
Permanent development makes small durable changes.
Exactly one race package may be active per Grand Prix.
Weekend setup redistributes performance rather than creating free performance.
Headline ratings are player-facing summaries; simulation uses detailed ratings.
The 2026 active-aero system is represented through speed and aero attributes rather than a separate Active Aero stat.
The increased importance of electrical energy is represented inside Acceleration / Deployment rather than a separate ERS stat.

headlineAttributes.label: Speed
headlineAttributes.description: Straight-line performance and the ability to accelerate and deploy electrical energy effectively.

headlineAttributes.label: Cornering
headlineAttributes.description: Aerodynamic performance through both fast and slow corners.

headlineAttributes.label: Mechanical Grip
headlineAttributes.description: Chassis performance under braking, rotation and traction, especially where aero is less dominant.

headlineAttributes.label: Tyres
headlineAttributes.description: Ability to preserve tyres and keep them inside a useful operating window.

headlineAttributes.label: Reliability
headlineAttributes.description: Resistance to mechanical problems and performance loss across demanding race weekends.

detailedAttributes.label: Top Speed
detailedAttributes.description: Maximum straight-line capability after accounting for drag, active-aero efficiency and gearing/power characteristics.

detailedAttributes.label: Acceleration / Deployment
detailedAttributes.description: Acceleration out of corners and the ability to deploy hybrid electrical energy effectively across a lap and race phase.

detailedAttributes.label: High-Speed Aero
detailedAttributes.description: Downforce, efficiency and stability through high-speed corners in Corner Mode.

detailedAttributes.label: Low-Speed Aero
detailedAttributes.description: Aerodynamic support, rotation and balance in slower corners where aero load is reduced.

detailedAttributes.label: Mechanical Grip
detailedAttributes.description: Underlying chassis and suspension grip independent of pure aerodynamic load.

detailedAttributes.label: Braking
detailedAttributes.description: Braking stability, controllability and confidence during heavy deceleration and corner entry.

detailedAttributes.label: Traction
detailedAttributes.description: Ability to put power down effectively on corner exit without excessive wheelspin or instability.

detailedAttributes.label: Tyre Wear
detailedAttributes.description: Ability of the car to preserve tyre performance over a stint. Higher values mean lower degradation for equivalent driving.

detailedAttributes.label: Tyre Temperature
detailedAttributes.description: Ability to bring tyres into and keep them within the useful operating window in both cold and hot conditions.

detailedAttributes.label: Reliability
detailedAttributes.description: Resistance to component faults, overheating, derating and race-ending failures.

trackFitModel.description: Each track's detailed demand value acts as the importance weight for the matching car attribute. Reliability is resolved separately against track mechanical stress.

reliabilityInteraction.effect: Higher mechanical stress magnifies the consequence of low reliability; it should not directly reduce normal lap pace until a reliability event occurs.

referenceBaseline.purpose: Neutral tuning reference only; not a playable pre-built car.

preseasonArchitecture.guidance: Most preseason choices should look like +2/+1/-1 rather than extreme +3/0/-3 swings.

permanentDevelopment.guidance: Permanent upgrades are deliberately incremental so the season does not become an upgrade race.

racePackage.guidance: Race packages may be stronger than permanent upgrades because only one package can be active at a Grand Prix.

weekendSetup.guidance: Setup changes redistribute performance and should be near-zero-sum across the affected attributes.

axes.label: Aero
axes.notes: Because 2026 uses active front and rear aero, setup trade-offs should be meaningful but less binary than a traditional fixed-wing high/low-downforce model.

axes.label: Mechanical
axes.notes: This axis also feeds driver-preference compatibility; responsive setups favour drivers seeking rotation, stable setups favour drivers seeking rear confidence.

axes.label: Tyres
axes.notes: Warm-up setup improves immediate tyre readiness but consumes more tyre life; preservation does the reverse.

driverCompatibilityDimensions.description: How immediate and assertive the front axle feels on turn-in.
Rear confidence during braking, rotation and traction phases.
How readily the car rotates into and through slower corners.
Stability and confidence under heavy braking and initial turn-in.
Predictability and grip when applying power on corner exit.
Confidence in the car's rear and aero platform through fast corners.

implementationNotes: Store detailed ratings as authoritative performance values; derive headline ratings at runtime or during seed validation.
Apply base architecture, permanent development, race package and setup as separate modifier layers before clamping the effective detailed rating.
Do not permanently mutate the base-car rating when applying a race package or weekend setup.
Recommended effective-rating clamp for initial balancing is 60-100.
Reliability should drive probability/severity of faults rather than act as a constant lap-time modifier.
Driver technical skill should improve setup information and adaptation, not directly add raw car rating points.
Driver preferences should create small compatibility effects; Adaptability should reduce mismatch penalties.
